resolutions.pipeline_name: Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines
resolutions.researcher_notes: GulfPub 'Badr el Din 2 - Badr el Din' trace (26.8 km) matches the BED-2->BED-3 corridor the research corroborated. BAPETCO's BED concession (Abu Gharadig basin, ~300 km west of Cairo per nsenergybusiness.com) contains numbered sub-fields BED-1/BED-2/BED-3, developed together as one cluster. Farmout Angel's coordinates for BED-2 and BED-3 are mutually consistent (~25 km apart) and closely match GulfPub's cited 26.8 km 'Badr el Din 2 - Badr el Din' trace -- the strongest evidence found for what this 'Spur (1)' pipeline actually connects. Deliberately did NOT use the payload's facility_anchor coordinate for 'Bed-2 Oil and Gas Field (Matrouh, Egypt)' (lon=26.66, lat=30.26): it sits ~190 km WNW of the BED-1/BED-3 cluster, geographically implausible for a field developed as part of the same concession as BED-3 -- flagging this as a likely mismapped coordinate in the internal GOGET dataset, not a basis for a route. Single-source coordinates (Farmout Angel) for both endpoints; a second independent geocoding source would strengthen this further, but the distance/order-of-magnitude match to GulfPub's trace gives reasonable confidence. No dedicated Arabic-language article found describing this specific spur by name. SHEET CONFLICT: Sheet gives 130.0 km for this spur; independent coordinates for BED-2 and BED-3 put a two-point great-circle distance at ~25 km, which sits inside the disputed-range window the prior researcher flagged (GulfPub reports comparable BED lines at 19-63 km, with a specific 'Badr el Din 2 - Badr el Din Pipeline' trace of 26.8 km matching this corridor closely). The sheet's 130 km figure looks materially overstated for this corridor. Suggest StartLocation -> 'Badr El Din 2 (BED-2) Field'. Suggest EndLocation -> 'Badr El Din 3 (BED-3) gas processing facility'.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines
resolutions.researcher_notes: GulfPub 'Badr el Din Field - Alam El Shawish' trace (70 km) matches the BED-3->Alam El Shawish corridor the research corroborated. Two-point candidate uses BED-3 (documented tie-in hub) and the Alam El Shawish West concession centroid; straight-line distance is only ~16 km, well under both GulfPub's 70 km trace and the ~47 km summed pipeline-segment figure from Egypt Oil & Gas -- expected, since concession-block centroids don't reflect actual routing across a ~1,075 km2 block to specific well clusters (Assil/Karam sit within, not necessarily at, the block centroid). A separate Egypt Oil & Gas piece ('Field Development back on track') independently confirms Alam El Shawish and Badr El-Din are linked by transport infrastructure (for crude oil rather than this gas spur), corroborating the two fields as pipeline-connected neighbors. On the P3937/P3938 duplicate question: found evidence these are TWO DISTINCT real corridors radiating from the BED-3 hub in different directions (P3937 west/short to BED-2, P3938 west-southwest to Alam El Shawish/Assil-Karam) -- not duplicates of each other -- but the sheet's shared, unverified 130 km length for both looks like a data error that should be corrected downward for both rows rather than treated as ground truth. Confidence: moderate -- endpoint identification and general corridor direction are reasonably corroborated by 2+ independent sources (Farmout Angel coordinates + Egypt Oil & Gas pipeline description), but exact routing/length remains uncertain. SHEET CONFLICT: Sheet gives 130.0 km, identical to P3937's figure for a completely different corridor -- the two rows sharing the exact same length looks like a duplication/copy error rather than two independently measured pipelines. Egypt Oil & Gas ('Assil and Karam fields on the development track') documents real gathering pipelines from the Alam El Shawish West concession's Assil/Karam gas development tying into BED-3: a 24 km 12-in line, a 12 km 12-in line, and an 11.3 km 8-in line (~47 km summed across segments) -- same order of magnitude as GulfPub's cited 70 km 'Badr el Din Field - Alam El Shawish' trace, and far short of the sheet's 130 km. Likely origin of the '130' figure: an unrelated Oil & Gas Journal CO2-EOR study describes gathering CO2-rich gas from four DIFFERENT Western Desert plants (Obaiyed, El Salam, Tarek, El Qasr) to a central point in El Salam, then piping it 130 MILES (not km) to Abu Sennan field for storage -- a different corridor entirely (El Salam-to-Abu Sennan, not BED-to-Alam El Shawish) and a proposed/study concept, not confirmed built infrastructure. Plausible the sheet's '130' for both BED spurs is a garbled echo of this unrelated 130-mile CO2 study number rather than a real measurement of either spur. Suggest StartLocation -> 'Badr El Din 3 (BED-3) gas processing facility'. Suggest EndLocation -> 'Alam El Shawish West field/concession'.

Could not source a precise wellhead coordinate for Karawan itself from any independent source; used the documented 'Temsah' field entry (same concession) as a concession-area start anchor, and Port Said (Wikipedia) as a named shore anchor for the export tie-in end. Both anchors are corroborated as being in the right offshore-Mediterranean-near-Port-Said geography by 2+ independent sources; the exact coordinates themselves each come from a single geocoding source. Length (206 km) remains an open, likely-erroneous, single-sourced figure -- flagged, not resolved. By contrast, the offshore DEKA/Karawan/Temsah-Concession/Petrobel/32-inch-export-tie-in/El-Gamil-plant story is corroborated by two independent English trade sources (egyptoil-gas.com, offshore-mag.com) plus the row's own existing Arabic ref (almalnews.com), and its Operator field (Belayim Petroleum Co = Petrobel) matches the DEKA operator exactly -- strong evidence the row's underlying real-world asset is the Karawan-field sealine, filed under a mistranslated/conflated name.
